cards.headline: From Bali to Hoi An, how a family turned the world into their classroom
bullets: A Singaporean family of six travelled for months, turning the world into their classroom.
They explored places like Bali and Hoi An as part of their unique learning approach.
This extended travel served as an alternative lifestyle and educational method for the family.

cards.headline: Pig’s blood is back on the menu. But is Singapore hungry for it?
bullets: Pig's blood is now allowed back in Singapore after a 27-year ban.
The ban was put in place in 1999 due to the Nipah virus outbreak.
Pig's blood was a key ingredient in some traditional dishes, like organ soup.
Some hawkers are considering bringing back pig's blood to their menus.

cards.headline: How can I best support my son to ensure he stays focused and confident for the PSLE?
bullets: Parents can help their sons stay focused for the PSLE by providing a stable and supportive home.
Ensure your child gets enough rest to maintain confidence during the exam period.
The PSLE Companion microsite offers more tips for parents.
Experts suggest creating a well-rested environment for children.

cards.headline: Racist, hateful comments towards Indians are deeply troubling; S’poreans must reject hatred: SM Lee
bullets: SM Lee says racist remarks against Indians are troubling and must be rejected.
Comments were made after the Nepal flood tragedy and linked to Air India investment.
Some remarks used racist stereotypes and attacked Temasek's CEO.
Leaders must condemn hate speech to protect Singapore's racial harmony.
Police are investigating the racist and xenophobic comments.

cards.headline: Audition for ChildAid, David Attenborough VR show at ArtScience Museum, The Courage To Be You book
bullets: Adults can now audition with kids for the ChildAid charity fund-raiser.
A new VR show at ArtScience Museum lets you see life 3.5 billion years ago.
A new book, The Courage To Be You, helps kids with self-doubt.
ChildAid 2026 is now an outdoor event at UOB Plaza on Nov 13-14.

cards.headline: Everyone needs a death to-do list – here are 25 things to sort out while you're alive
bullets: Over half of Singaporeans haven't discussed or written down their final wishes.
Planning your funeral, like wake length and cremation, helps loved ones avoid guessing.
Appointing someone to lead your funeral and give a eulogy reduces family confusion.
A will can protect children and pets, and name guardians for them.
Leaving a letter of wishes explains why you divided assets or made specific choices.

cards.headline: Singapore air quality improves to moderate range after unhealthy readings
bullets: Air quality improved to moderate levels on Saturday after being unhealthy earlier.
The central region saw PSI drop from 123 to 91 overnight.
West and east regions also returned to moderate air quality.
North and south regions stayed in the moderate range all day.
Haze may continue if fires in Indonesia persist.

cards.headline: One person taken to hospital after Simon Lane house fire
bullets: A fire broke out at a house on Simon Lane on Saturday afternoon.
One person was taken to hospital for smoke inhalation.
About 30 people from nearby homes were evacuated.
Firefighters put out the blaze, with some neighbours' homes also affected.

cards.headline: Racism has no place in Singapore; concerns about SIA-Air India deal ‘purely commercial’, says WP MP Kenneth Tiong
bullets: MP Kenneth Tiong says racism has no place in Singapore.
He states his concerns about SIA's Air India deal are purely commercial.
Tiong condemned racist online comments about the deal.
He believes tough questions about money and racism should not be mixed.

cards.headline: Police looking into 'shameful' racist online comments about Nepal-Tibet disaster, Air India: SM Shanmugam
bullets: Police are investigating shameful racist online comments about the Nepal-Tibet disaster.
Senior Minister Shanmugam called the comments unacceptable and vowed to unmask those responsible.
Online racism has also targeted Singapore Airlines' investment in Air India.
MP Alex Yam described the racist remarks about missing Singaporeans as heartless.

cards.headline: Mbappe denied at the death as Betis beat Real Madrid
bullets: Real Betis beat Real Madrid 1-0, ending Madrid's perfect start to the season.
Substitute Troy Parrott scored the winning goal for Betis nine minutes from the end.
Betis goalkeeper Alvaro Valles saved Kylian Mbappe's penalty in stoppage time.
Mbappe also hit the crossbar earlier in the second half.

cards.headline: Early Isak double leads Liverpool to victory at Ipswich
bullets: Liverpool beat Ipswich 2-0 with two early goals from Alexander Isak.
Cody Gakpo assisted both of Isak's goals in the first nine minutes.
New signing Bradley Barcola made his debut for Liverpool in the second half.
Liverpool secured their first win of the season under new manager Andoni Iraola.

cards.headline: GWM Ora 5 review: Instead of adrenaline, this EV activates a different hormone
bullets: The GWM Ora 5 electric car has a cute, retro design that aims to make drivers smile.
It offers a 435 km range, enough for a week of normal driving, with a 136 horsepower motor.
The interior is bright and welcoming, but the beige seats might be hard to keep clean.
While not sporty, the ride is comfortable, and it handles city driving well.
The car's touchscreen menu system can be confusing to navigate.

cards.headline: Beijing’s tax crackdown tests wealthy Chinese property buyers in Singapore
bullets: China is taxing offshore trusts by 20%, affecting wealthy Chinese property buyers in Singapore.
This tax move makes wealthy Chinese reconsider where they keep their assets.
Agents report some worry but no major sell-off of Singapore properties.
Beijing is increasing efforts to collect taxes on overseas income and profits.

cards.headline: Eu Yan Sang family members sell Bishopsgate bungalow for S$40 million
bullets: Eu Yan Sang family members sold a bungalow for S$40 million.
The Bishopsgate property has a land area of about 16,124 square feet.
The buyer is reportedly a family member of Nippon Paint Holdings director Wee Siew Kim.

cards.headline: Woodlands North station ready, another step closer to Johor Bahru-S'pore RTS Link opening
bullets: Woodlands North station for the RTS Link is ready four months early.
The station's design reflects Woodlands' nature identity with tree-inspired colours.
Building the station involved overcoming challenges like blasting hard rock.
Commuters will clear immigration once before boarding the 5-minute train ride to Johor Bahru.
The RTS Link aims to carry 10,000 passengers per hour between the countries.

cards.headline: S'pore actor & content creator Wilfred Lee passes away aged 26
bullets: Local actor and content creator Wilfred Lee died at 26.
He reportedly passed away peacefully in his sleep.
Lee was known for his videos exploring Singapore and food reviews.
His wake is from Sep. 5 to Sep. 7, with cremation on Sep. 7.

cards.headline: US woman, 41, poses as sister of Marriott staff to get discounted rates for 14 nights at Sheraton Towers S'pore
bullets: An American woman got over S$1,500 in hotel discounts by pretending to be a Marriott staff's sister.
She stayed 14 nights at Sheraton Towers Singapore using fake membership details bought online.
The hotel found out she wasn't related to the staff after she checked out.
She pleaded guilty to cheating and has returned the money.

cards.headline: 13 Unique Bus Stops In Singapore, From Experimental Stops To Ones With Quirky Designs
bullets: Some bus stops in Singapore have unique designs, unlike typical shelters.
The S'goon Gdn Circus bus stop serves buses going in both directions on the same platform.
The Masjid Kassim bus stop is painted emerald green and has a glass roof section.
The Synergy bus stop looks like a UFO with its dome-shaped roof.
Two bus stops are built inside car parks: one at Kranji Reservoir and another near East Coast Park.

cards.headline: All You Need To Know About The Upcoming Wetlands By The Bay, Featuring A New teamLab Museum
bullets: Construction for Wetlands by the Bay starts in early 2027, with openings expected by late 2028.
A new 5ha nature attraction, Wetlands by the Bay, is coming to Gardens by the Bay.
It will feature a large new teamLab digital art museum, bigger than the one at ArtScience Museum.
A 550m bridge will connect Bay South and Bay East Gardens, including a section over the reservoir.
Satay by the Bay will close in September 2026 to make way for a new two-storey dining area.
